newsitem.title: USA: Reuters says change is continuous process.
newsitem.headline: Reuters says change is continuous process.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc Chief Executive Officer Peter Job told a PaineWebber media conference on Wednesday that rationalization of the company's businesses is a continuous process.
But Job said the company has not done any major restructuring since 1992. He said the company is not likely to have any big restructurings in the future which would involve charges to earnings.
"You can rely on us not to do that," Job said, speaking by videoconference.
Asked about cost control and headcount, Job referred to the company's "continuous initiatives," which he said are necessary for a company that has grown very fast in a rapidly changing business.
He did not cite any figures for headcount, but said there had recently been a move to shift administrative and central staff positions to "customer-facing positions."
He said his comments included the operations in the United States.

Reuters will lay off about 170 staff in the Americas as a result of organizational changes designed to streamline the American operation and make it more efficient and sales-driven, Reuters America Holdings Inc spokesman Robert Crooke said.

The cuts, most of which will have taken place by mid-January, amount to about five percent of the company's American workforce of 3,500 and affect sales, marketing, editorial, technical, finance and administrative staff.
Job told the meeting that the company is a heavy investor in research and development, committing seven percent of revenue to such activity.
Asked about the company's cash hoard, he said any acquisitions the company made would likely be small.
He noted that British law has prevented the company from distributing the cash to shareholders as it would like to do.
He identified several business areas the company looks on with favor, including the Internet and the U.S. fixed-income and equity markets.
